text:
mike: Heads-up from ingestion ops: EU late-window spikes again this morning, lots of 2-4h lagged events. The recompute queue is filling and the console heatmap shows 'long-tail' token latency on shared pools. Thinking we should try spot fallback routing for low-priority replays to avoid blocking live requests. Thoughts?

tara: Can we define 'low-priority' precisely? Right now some targeted replays are marked important by sales. We need a deterministic rule: maybe `replay.priority=background || tenant.meta.backfill_ok=true`.

ben: Agree on deterministic. Also add a TTL: if replay.window_end < now()-2h then mark background. That captures obvious late-arrival bulk workloads.

mike: Good idea. Example log line we saw:
```
INGEST-ALERT: shard=eu-west hour=2026-03-01T05:00Z lag=10800 count=1200
REPLAY: enqueue id=rp-20260301-22 tenant=acme window=2h reason=late-arrive
```

replay-bot: New replay scheduled: rp-20260301-22 (tenant=acme) status=queued estimated_tokens=1.1M

ops: If we route to spot-dedicated pools we need two things: 1) quota checks + a quick user-visible cost warning in console for reserved-slot use, 2) telemetry labels so billing and aggregate freshness metrics don't get double-counted.

lina: UX: I'd rather show a subtle toggle: "Use lower-cost spot pool if available (may be preempted)" with an inline tooltip linking to docs. We should show estimated wait-time delta and estimated cost delta. Who owns the estimate calc?

ben: Backend: scheduling can return a cost_estimate object in the replay create response. Minimal format: `{"tokens": n, "est_cost": "$x", "wait_ms_p50": 300000}`. Console can render that.

tara: We need to avoid priority inversion where a flood of small background replays starve medium-priority ones due to batching behavior. Proposal: routing policy should incorporate `batch_size` and `expected_token_rate` and apply an admission control threshold. E.g. background lane max concurrent tokens = 5M tokens across region.

mike: Good call. Also add a safety: if foreground SLO breaches (p95 latency > 300ms) automatically throttle background lane by 50% and spill to spot pools or passive queue.

ops: Can we implement a temporary soft-scheduling label for this morning while we test? Something like `tier_hint=spot_fallback` that scheduler honors if available. Use feature flag `routing.spot_fallback=true` in staging --> then 1-tenant canary.

lina: I'll add the toggle in the modal but behind a feature flag too. UX will also show a CTA to request quota for dedicated spot pools if estimate > threshold.

mike: I'll add the `tier_hint` to the internal API. Example curl: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/replays -H 'Auth: Bearer $T' -d '{"tenant":"acme","window":"2h","tier_hint":"spot_fallback"}'`

replay-bot: rp-20260301-22 status=scheduled pool=shared (pending spot assignment)

ben: Two telemetry asks: 1) add `replay.routing.tier` tag (values: shared, dedicated, spot) to all replay metrics; 2) add `replay.backfill.reason` for downstream aggregate freshness dashboards so we can filter recomputes from live drift.

ops: We'll need to update alerting: separate SLOs for shared vs dedicated pools so noisy background jobs don't pollute SLOs for live API. Also add a dashboard panel that correlates replay token volumes vs API p95.

mike: Quick rollout plan: 1) scheduler accepts `tier_hint` behind ff; 2) console exposes toggle behind ff; 3) enable in staging and run a 2-hour canary with a single non-critical tenant; 4) monitor p95 and token burn; 5) if stable, roll to EU region.

tara: One more caveat: dedupe. If late-arrival causes duplicate keys we might waste tokens rehydrating the same aggregates. Let's run a small dedupe pass in the pre-scheduler check: sample keys and skip known-processed keys within X window. That reduces wasted replays.

ben: Agree. Add `precheck.dedupe=true` option, default off, enabled for spot_fallback canary. If dedupe hits >30% skip rate, increase background lane capacity since jobs are cheaper.

mike: I'll open PRs for scheduler + telemetry tags. Lina/Tara pair on console + dedupe precheck config. Ops please queue a quota request for spot-dedicated pool if needed.

ops: Will do `rb-tool quota request --tenant acme --pool spot-dedicated-eu --tokens 1200000 --hours 2` and link back. We'll monitor.

replay-bot: rp-20260301-22 status=running pool=spot-dedicated workers=4 precheck.dedupe=true

lina: Canary looks clean so far, p95 API latency unchanged. Small note: console tooltip should say "may be preempted; retries will fallback to shared pool".

mike: Great. If this works, we can add a routing policy DSL to codify `tier_hint` behavior and expose a simple UI for ops to configure soft caps.

ben: Agreed, forwarding to RFC to capture batch-size + token caps + telemetry changes. I'll draft RFC and ping infra-reviewers.

mike: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the 2h canary to decide next steps.
